source.title: Can LLMs Truly Forget? Revealing Unlearning Gaps Through Adversarial Evaluation
source.authors: A. Gupta; Hima Varshini Surisetty; Sreevidya Bollineni; Varad Ingale; Tuhina Tripathi; Abhishek Lalwani; Somya Chatterjee; Sadid A. Hasan

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether fine-tuning-based unlearning remains vulnerable to adversarial prompting, and reports that recovery rates are close to the unprotected model’s rate. This challenges the idea that strong clean-query forgetting establishes resistance to recovery.
record.gate_note: The paper tests adversarial prompting and clean multilingual reformulations, not fine-tuning on a small recovery set, activation-direction ablation or mechanism analysis, or quantization. It reports clean-query Forget Quality and Model Utility, but those metrics are not targeted-knowledge accuracy and do not themselves establish recovery; no separate rows are included for them. Table 3 is an illustrative example already represented by the attack-suite results, not a separate condition. Table 5's judge/ROUGE correlation is metric validation, not a recovery result.
record.test_reason: The study applies REBEL-style adversarial prompting and clean multilingual probes to NPO, SimNPO, AltPO and RMU models. These models score high on clean-query Forget Quality on TOFU, and the study reports how often forget-set answers leak. Its numbers bear directly on whether prompting recovers the knowledge (E) and whether those methods resist simple attacks (A).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that high clean-query Forget Quality does not imply resistance to recovery: adversarial English prompts give ASRs of 72.8–84.3%, near the base model's 87.5%, while clean multilingual probes leak only 2.95%. ASR is a useful but imperfect signal (7/10 audit agreement). The paraphrase omits a second finding: prompt-based methods' Forget Quality collapses as the forget set grows under unified evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates NPO, SimNPO, AltPO, and RMU on TOFU and applies REBEL-style adversarial prompts; it does not test the original claim's fine-tuning recovery set, activation ablation, quantization, or all listed unlearning methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack formulation changes outcomes: Multiple Choice has the lowest ASRs (45.0%–70.0%), while Authority and System Injection are 82.5%–90.0% across methods. Clean multilingual leakage also varies by language, with German highest and Arabic, Hindi, and Japanese reported at 0.0%.

fits_no_version.finding: Prompt-based unlearning (SPUL, ICUL) looks effective under author-reported Forget Accuracy but collapses to near-zero Forget Quality at the 5%/10% splits under OpenUnlearning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The apparent efficacy of unlearning depends on the evaluation metric; token-level accuracy overstates the effect of prompt-based methods.

record.problems: Only Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct is tested; adversarial evaluation is limited to the 1% TOFU split and synthetic biographies. ASR depends on an LLM judge and a fixed 0.2 threshold; a purposive audit by one annotator agrees on seven of ten cases. The multilingual ROUGE-L threshold was not calibrated against human judgments.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, multilingual language-by-method entries were omitted for all Japanese conditions and for RMU on Hindi; the other Hindi entries are retained. The omitted entries are 0.0% in Table 6. Clean-query FQ/MU table entries were not extracted as rows because they do not directly measure the attack-recovery outcomes at issue; their relevance is summarized in gate_note.

untested.parts: Near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy is not measured; Forget Quality is a distributional similarity score. General ability is checked only via TOFU Model Utility. Adversarial tests cover only the 1% split and one 3B model.
No activation ablation or mechanistic analysis.
In-context information attacks, multi-turn and gradient-based prompts, and other model families are not tested.
No robust counter-method is proposed or tested.

record.verdict_notes: The main interpretive caveat is that ASR for the unlearned models on plain English forget questions is never reported. The near-plain 'Direct' suite scores about as high as jailbreak-style suites, so the gap may reflect Forget Quality failing to capture generation-level leakage rather than prompting recovering hidden knowledge. The judge also flags plausible but wrong answers as leakage (audit samples S02, S05), which inflates ASR. The 0.2 threshold is uncalibrated. Results come from a single 3B model on synthetic TOFU data at the 1% split only.

versions.untested_parts: Tests adversarial recovery after fine-tuning-based methods with strong clean-query Forget Quality, on the 1% forget split. It does not establish near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy or test recovery after every unlearning method or forget split.
No recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis showing that a method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Tests eight adversarial English attack suites and clean queries translated into seven languages. Does not test every rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context-information strategy.
No newer counter-method is proposed and tested for resistance to these attacks.
